<h3>Quiz 1: The Central Limit Theorem <span id="quiz-done-w6_q_clt" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the coffee shop example, individual waiting times follow a right-skewed Gamma distribution. What does the Central Limit Theorem say about the distribution of <em>sample means</em> of waiting times as the sample size n grows?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt1" id="clt1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt1a">It stays right-skewed, just like the individual waiting times</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt1" id="clt1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt1b">It becomes approximately normal, regardless of the shape of the original distribution</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt1" id="clt1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt1c">It becomes uniform</label></div>
    <div id="clt1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What is one essential condition for the Central Limit Theorem to hold?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt2" id="clt2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt2a">The original variable must already be normally distributed</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt2" id="clt2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt2b">The individual random variables being averaged must be independent of each other</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt2" id="clt2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt2c">The sample size must be exactly 30</label></div>
    <div id="clt2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Looking at the Q-Q plots for n = 2, n = 10 and n = 200 sample means, what pattern do you see?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt3" id="clt3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt3a">The fit to the normal line gets worse as n increases</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt3" id="clt3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt3b">The fit to the normal line gets better as n increases, becoming almost perfect at n = 200</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="clt3" id="clt3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="clt3c">n has no effect on the Q-Q plot</label></div>
    <div id="clt3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkCltQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="clt-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Standard Error &amp; Sample Size <span id="quiz-done-w6_q_se" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does the formula <code>SE = σ / √n</code> tell you?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se1" id="se1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="se1a">The standard error shrinks as the sample size n grows</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se1" id="se1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="se1b">The standard error grows as the sample size n grows</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se1" id="se1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="se1c">The standard error is independent of n</label></div>
    <div id="se1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> The exercise notes "diminishing returns": going from n=10 to n=20 helps more than going from n=80 to n=90. Why?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se2" id="se2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="se2a">Because SE depends on √n, so each additional observation reduces SE less and less at larger n</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se2" id="se2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="se2b">Because R has a bug for large sample sizes</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se2" id="se2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="se2c">Because the mean changes at large n</label></div>
    <div id="se2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Does the <em>mean</em> of the sample means change as the sample size n increases?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se3" id="se3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="se3a">No — it stays centered on the true population mean; only the spread (SE) shrinks</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se3" id="se3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="se3b">Yes — it increases proportionally with n</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="se3" id="se3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="se3c">Yes — it decreases proportionally with n</label></div>
    <div id="se3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkSeQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="se-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Confidence Intervals <span id="quiz-done-w6_q_ci" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does a "95% confidence interval" mean?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci1" id="ci1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci1a">There is a 95% probability that any single observation falls in this range</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci1" id="ci1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci1b">If we repeated the sampling many times, about 95% of the constructed intervals would contain the true population parameter</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci1" id="ci1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci1c">The sample mean is wrong 95% of the time</label></div>
    <div id="ci1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> In the coffee-cup example (n = 9 cups), why do we use the <strong>t-distribution</strong> with 8 degrees of freedom rather than the normal distribution to compute the critical value?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci2" id="ci2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci2a">Because the sample size is small, and the true standard deviation is unknown and estimated from the sample</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci2" id="ci2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci2b">Because coffee cup volumes are always t-distributed</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci2" id="ci2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci2c">Because degrees of freedom only apply to normal distributions</label></div>
    <div id="ci2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Comparing a 90% CI and a 95% CI computed from the same data, which one is wider?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci3" id="ci3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci3a">The 90% CI is wider</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci3" id="ci3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci3b">The 95% CI is wider — higher confidence requires a larger margin</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ci3" id="ci3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ci3c">They are always exactly the same width</label></div>
    <div id="ci3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkCiQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="ci-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 4: Plenum Demos — CLT in Action <span id="quiz-done-w6_q_plenum" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the dice-sum ("Augensumme") plenum demo, rolling 2 dice and averaging over N repeated pairs of rolls, what happens to the distribution of the averaged sum as N grows from 1 to 100?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd1" id="pd1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd1a">It stays exactly the same, uniformly spread between 2 and 12</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd1" id="pd1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd1b">It becomes increasingly concentrated and bell-shaped around the theoretical mean of 7</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd1" id="pd1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd1c">It becomes more spread out and skewed</label></div>
    <div id="pd1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> In the chocolate-bar weight demo, individual error sources (weighing cocoa, weighing sugar, ...) are each <strong>uniformly</strong> distributed on [-1, 1]. What happens to the distribution of the total error once you sum up 100 such independent uniform error sources?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd2" id="pd2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd2a">It stays uniformly distributed, just wider</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd2" id="pd2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd2b">It becomes approximately normally distributed — confirmed by the Q-Q plot lying on the diagonal</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd2" id="pd2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd2c">It becomes a Poisson distribution</label></div>
    <div id="pd2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> The plenum repeats the "mean of N samples" experiment starting from Normal, Poisson and t-distributed data. What is the common conclusion across all of them?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd3" id="pd3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd3a">Only data that starts out normal ends up with normal sample means</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd3" id="pd3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd3b">Regardless of the starting distribution, the sample means concentrate around the true mean with a spread shrinking like 1/√N — the CLT in action</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pd3" id="pd3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pd3c">The sample mean is unrelated to the true mean</label></div>
    <div id="pd3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkPlenumCltQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="plenum-clt-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<h3 style="margin-top:1.5rem;">Quiz 3: Confidence Intervals <span style="font-size:0.8rem;color:#7c9cef;font-weight:normal;">(scipy.stats.t.interval)</span></h3>
<div class="placeholder-card">
  <p style="color:#7c9cef;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:1rem;">🐍 Python Quiz — Coming Soon</p>
  <div style="opacity:0.65;">
    <p><strong>Preview Question:</strong> Which scipy.stats function directly returns a confidence interval for a t-distribution?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" disabled=""><label class="form-check-label" style="color:#888;"><code>t.interval()</code></label></div>
